summary: Changsha fits high-energy food and nightlife travel shaped by street-level eating, riverside evenings, youth-heavy districts, and practical urban routing.
transport_notes: Changsha works best when plans stay within one central old-city or river-adjacent zone per day.
Metro plus short walks is practical, but nightlife-heavy plans should avoid long late-night cross-city transfers.
Evening pacing is strongest around riverside promenades, food streets, and lively central neighborhoods.

budget_notes.low: Prioritize snack streets, public riverside areas, and compact central neighborhoods with dense food options.
budget_notes.medium: Blend one signature street area, one scenic or cultural stop, and one stronger evening food district each day.
budget_notes.high: Add slower dining, more comfort in movement, and selective riverside or skyline evening moments.

trip_type_notes.student: Student plans in Changsha should emphasize nightlife energy, affordable local food, and easy central-city execution.
trip_type_notes.solo: Solo plans should balance food exploration with enough slower city observation and riverfront breathing room.
trip_type_notes.couple: Couple plans should use Changsha's lights and food culture without making the whole trip feel rushed or noisy.
trip_type_notes.family: Family plans should avoid overly late-night routes and favor easier scenic or cultural anchors with manageable food areas.
